statement: migrate_legacy_name's JSON/TOML rewrite (rewrite_json/rewrite_toml) touches ONLY the structured mcpServers.<LEGACY_SERVER_NAME>/mcp_servers.<LEGACY_SERVER_NAME> registration KEY, never a global substring replace over the serialized file. A global raw.replace("ocentra-enforcer", "enforcer") over the whole JSON/TOML text would also mangle an unrelated field VALUE that happens to contain the literal (e.g. a command path pointing at an old-but-still-present /usr/local/bin/ocentra-enforcer binary, or any user data string). The global substring rewrite (rewrite_text) is reserved for ConfigFormat::ManagedText files only (e.g. Codex's AGENTS.md doctrine block), which have no field-value/name-surface distinction to preserve. scan_json/scan_toml mirror this exact key-only scope so scan and rewrite never disagree about what counts as legacy residue.
why: Caught via a failing test: the first fixture draft's Claude adapter command value was literally "/usr/local/bin/ocentra-enforcer", and a naive whole-file rewrite silently changed that path's bytes too -- which would corrupt a real user's already-registered binary path on a live migration, not just a cosmetic rename. This is a correctness-critical distinction for any future adapter/format x03 (or a x03-adjacent doctor/migrate caller) adds to the ConfigTarget list.
howToApply: When adding a new ConfigFormat variant (a new harness's structured config), scan/rewrite its LEGACY_SERVER_NAME only via the structured key path (parse -> get/remove/insert on the specific key), never via a raw string replace over the whole serialized document. Only apply the raw substring rewrite (rewrite_text/scan_text_literals) to genuinely free-text/prose surfaces that have no structured key of their own.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-install/src/migrate_legacy_name.rs rewrite_json/rewrite_toml/rewrite_text; pass_fixture_claude_migrate_rewrites_legacy_entry_to_enforcer caught the bug when asserting the post-migration command value

statement: x03's migrate_legacy_name module deliberately does NOT touch enforcer_mcp::registry::CANONICAL_TOOLS or enforcer_mcp::aliases (crate::aliases::CANONICAL_TOOL_PREFIX="ocentra_enforcer"/LEGACY_ALIAS_PREFIX="rust_rules") -- those are the LIVE MCP server's own still-current internal tool-registry family, a distinct not-yet-landed cutover x01 explicitly deferred (see mem-x01-0001) and x03's owns: line (only crates/enforcer-install/src/migrate_legacy_name.rs + its fixtures) does not grant. x03 only rewrites ALREADY-INSTALLED on-disk harness config files (the mcpServers/mcp_servers registration KEY, plus prose tool-name literals inside free-text managed blocks like AGENTS.md) so they name the MCP SERVER `enforcer` instead of the legacy `ocentra-enforcer` key -- it is a config-migration layer bolted onto core.rs's HarnessAdapter orchestration (core.rs's own doc comment: "x03 layers a legacy-name migration on top of an existing adapter rather than being an adapter itself"), not an adapter and not a rename of the live tool registry.
why: A future pack that eventually renames enforcer-mcp::registry::CANONICAL_TOOLS off the ocentra_enforcer_* family (the follow-up mem-x01-0001 flags) must NOT assume x03 already did that work just because x03's name says "rename migration" -- the two are unrelated surfaces (installed-config files vs the live server's own tool dispatch table) that happen to share vocabulary.
howToApply: Before assuming any tool-name-family rename is complete, check crates/enforcer-mcp/src/aliases.rs's deprecation_window_open() flag and CANONICAL_TOOL_PREFIX/LEGACY_ALIAS_PREFIX literals directly -- x03 landing does not change them.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-install/src/core.rs module doc ("x03 layers a legacy-name migration on top of an existing adapter"); crates/enforcer-mcp/src/aliases.rs; docs/plans/enforcer-selfhost-plan/workpacks/x03-rename-migration.md Parallel Ownership Notes ("It does not edit x01's name-source surfaces or sibling install adapter files")
